rows.verified: Exposure restriction should first use engineering controls and design features, with PPE relied on only as a last resort.
Work in an atmosphere above an annual average radon concentration of 300 Bq per cubic metre must be notified to HSE.
Workers likely to receive an effective dose above 6 mSv per year must be designated as classified persons under IRR17.
Ionising-radiation risk depends on source, activity, energy, distance, shielding, exposure time, pathway, controls and individual dose history.
HSE radiation evidence is source-, practice-, worker-, dose-, shielding-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer probability.
Employers have the same health, safety and welfare responsibilities for workers under 18 as for other workers.
For health and safety purposes, a young person is anyone under 18.
Young people may face greater injury risk during the first six months of a job because they are less familiar with workplace risks.
Additional vulnerability can arise from limited experience or maturity, incomplete physical maturity, eagerness to impress and uncertainty about raising concerns.
Young people need clear and sufficient instruction, training and supervision proportionate to the risk.
Young workers may require more supervision than adults while their capabilities and progress are established.
Risk assessments should be reviewed before employing a young person for the first time or one with particular needs.
Work-experience students are treated as employees for health and safety purposes, and the placement employer has primary responsibility.
Young-worker risk depends on age, maturity, experience, task, training, supervision, working hours, health and workplace culture.
HSE young-worker evidence is person-, task-, placement-, supervisor-, training-, workplace- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Employers must ensure employees receive immediate attention if they become ill or are injured at work.
Employers must assess workplace first-aid needs to decide what provision is appropriate.
Arrangements must include an appointed person or appropriate numbers of suitably trained first-aiders.
Employers must provide adequate first-aid facilities and a suitably stocked first-aid kit.
Employees must be informed about workplace first-aid arrangements.
Minimum provision includes a stocked kit, an appointed person and information for all employees.
The number of first-aiders should be determined from the employer's first-aid needs assessment.
Certain serious injuries, occupational diseases and dangerous occurrences must be reported under RIDDOR, and relevant records must be kept securely.
First-aid needs depend on workforce size, hazards, work patterns, remoteness, shift coverage, vulnerable people and emergency-service access.
HSE first-aid evidence is workplace-, workforce-, hazard-, shift-, responder-, facility- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level emergency-outcome probability.
